notice: Easy Mode dramatically simplifies the process of filter selection, an otherwise nuanced topic. Only a few of HQPlayer's filters are accessible here, so think of Easy Mode like training wheels and don't be afraid to experiment.

help.title: Easy Mode, explained
help.body:
Pick the preset that suits your material, then set its emphasis when available. The Perfect Ten, Lifelike, and Damage Control are the most all-purpose presets; Old School, The Purist, and Concert Hall are excellent with the appropriate material; The Crucible, Full Analog, and Textbook are curiosities for the sake of comparison.

'Transients' are sudden sounds like a snare drum hit or the leading edge of a plucked string. Choose for most multi-track studio recordings; such content often has an artificial sense of space but strong transient content. These filters emphasize clean transient reproduction.

Choose 'Space' for live or acoustic performances where the room or venue is part of the recording. The trade is slightly softer transients.

Note that the effect of these levers varies from preset to preset: for example, 'The Purist' adjusts the filter's length to change the emphasis; Old School, on the other hand, changes its phase.

When listening to high-rate material 88.2kHz or up, using The Perfect Ten or Lifelike gives you special filters for those rates.

When listening to lossy streams or files, use one of the presets with a Lossy mode (The Perfect Ten, Lifelike, and Damage Control); this gives you filters optimized for such content.

The glyphs (A) and (1/2) indicate the error correction level (apodizing); if no or half error correction sounds harsh or generates an apodizing events warning, try a different setting.

Pips estimate what a preset costs relative to the others on this card. The real load depends on your hardware, your output rate, and the rest of the chain, where the modulator or DAC correction can outweigh the filter entirely.

Still can't decide? Experiment! Presets can be changed live at any time with only a brief interruption to playback.

perfect-ten.title: The Perfect Ten
perfect-ten.description: Does everything well, no strings attached: the best-case solution to the tension at the heart of filter design.

lifelike.title: Lifelike
lifelike.description: Puts the focus on natural, realistic timbre.

old-school.title: Old School
old-school.description: Pairs well with classic-era analog recordings.

purist.title: The Purist
purist.description: Passes the original samples through unchanged. Only for the highest technical quality source material.

damage-control.title: Damage Control
damage-control.description: Aggressive clean-up; great for loudness war-era and other less-than-good material.

full-analog.title: Full Analog
full-analog.description: Imitates the smooth and relaxing sound of an analog playback chain.

textbook.title: Textbook
textbook.description: The sound of most standard-issue DAC hardware.

concert-hall.title: Concert Hall
concert-hall.description: Heavily emphasizes space over transients; for material like live classical with minimal transient content.

correction.label: Error correction
correction.tip: Disabling error correction reduces resource consumption.

crucible.title: The Crucible
crucible.description: Trial by fire: maximalist, brute-force signal reconstruction with no shortcuts.

correction.label: Error correction
correction.tip: Disabling error correction reduces resource consumption.
